subject: 52F3B40CB9B8EA39DE0F1D7A99B41677
introduction: These are prayers of Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking for detachment: “Grant me perfect detachment unto Thee”, “I am weary of self”, “Let me forget all but Thee”, “make me detached from all else save Thee”. Nearly all of them join the request to its purpose, to be attached to God, set free from “the bonds and fetters of self and passion”, and steadfast in service. The Psalmist’s “Whom have I in heaven but thee?”, Paul’s “I count all things but loss”, Rábi‘a’s “Thou art enough for me”, Ignatius’s “Take, Lord, and receive” and the Imitation of Christ pray in the same spirit. The Buddhist and Stoic teachers reach detachment without the love these prayers ask for: “those who love nothing … have no fetters”, “I have returned it”. Jesus’s “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world” and Tagore’s impatience with shut-in devotion ask what detachment is for.
questions: The prayers ask to be detached “from all else save Thee”. What is the difference between detachment from things and indifference to them?
The Dhammapada says to love nothing; these prayers ask for an overwhelming love. Compare the two paths. What does each fear?
Several prayers ask in one breath for detachment and for steadfast service. Why do the two belong together?
Reading 29 asks to be free of attachment “to friend and stranger alike”. What would that look like in a person who still loved their friends?
Which of these short prayers could you imagine using, and at what moments?

outside.why: A prayer to be wholly turned to God. Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.

“Grant me perfect detachment unto Thee.” Ignatius Loyola’s prayer of offering: take, Lord, and receive all my liberty, my memory, my intellect, and all my will. Give me Thy love and grace; that is enough for me.
“I am weary of self.” O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?
Free me from the bonds and fetters of self and passion. Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.

A prayer for a bounty that makes one independent of all else. Rábi‘a: whatever share of this world Thou hast allotted to me, bestow it on Thine enemies; and whatever share of the next, on Thy friends. Thou art enough for me.
Let me forget all but Thee. One thing have I desired of the Lord, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord.

“Intoxicated and bewildered from the cup of Thy love.” The Dhammapada’s detachment has no such cup: let no man love anything; those who love nothing and hate nothing, have no fetters. These prayers ask to be detached from all things by being attached to One. Is that a different freedom from the Buddha’s, or the same reached by another road?
To recognize Him and be severed from all else. I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord.
Purge from me the remembrance of anyone except Thee. Thomas à Kempis: vanity of vanities, all is vanity, except to love God, and only to serve Him.
A garden of Paradise heard from within this world. They confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth; they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly.
Deliver these souls from the world of fancy and guide them to reality. Plato’s prisoners, chained from childhood, who can only see before them the shadows on the wall.

Steadfast in service, and detached from this worldly existence. Jesus prays for his disciples: I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. How do these prayers keep detachment from becoming withdrawal?

Detached from all else, “speaking in Thy praise and standing firm in Thy service”. Tagore distrusts a piety that turns from the world: leave this chanting and singing and telling of beads! He is there where the tiller is tilling the hard ground. Would he object to these prayers, or find his own point in their second halves?
One who soars in the atmosphere of Thy love. They that wait upon the Lord shall mount up with wings as eagles.
Send down what will detach me from all else and draw me near. Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
The Name through which lovers soared and the yearning were consumed. Sa‘dí: O bird of the morning, learn love from the moth, because it burnt, lost its life, and found no voice.
Make them independent of all else save Thee. Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added unto you.
Detached from all else and holding fast to Thy Cord. Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
Free me from attachment to friend and stranger alike. Lovelace, from prison: if I have freedom in my love and in my soul am free, angels alone, that soar above, enjoy such liberty.

The Stoic’s detachment, by another method: never say of anything, “I have lost it”; but, “I have returned it.” Epictetus trains the judgement; the prayer asks to be “captivated” by love. Which do you find more believable as a way of holding one’s friends?
Deliver us from the transgressions of the past and the afflictions yet to come. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself.
Sever the cord of my attachment to all things. If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.
“I am he who hath detached himself from all else save Thee and hath fled to the shore of Thy mercy.” I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.

shortfall: Readings 7 to 12, 15, 17 to 28, 32 and 33 are petitions in one form (“I beseech Thee by … to make me detached from all else save Thee”) with different invocations; a companion was given where the petition adds something of its own, and ten of the thirty-four were left to the companions of the rest.
